rules.title: Housing Stability Notification Act (Notice of Tenants' Rights and Resources)
rules.requirement: Any landlord planning to end a tenancy must deliver a Notice of Tenants' Rights and Resources together with the Notice to quit or Notice of non-renewal of lease. Landlords and foreclosing owners must also submit tenant contact information and a copy of the notice to the City through an online portal. A violation does not halt the eviction process.
rules.key_value: Enforcement by Inspectional Services: 1st offense warning; 2nd and subsequent offenses $300 per day; failure to submit to City portal may result in fine up to $300 per day

coverage.summary: Applies to all landlords planning to end a tenancy agreement; no unit-count or building-age limits stated.

rules.effective_date_note: The page calls it the 'new' Act but gives no effective or enactment date.
rules.quoted_span:
The Housing Stability Notification Act requires
ALL LANDLORDS
planning to end a tenancy agreement to provide the tenant with a Notice of Tenants’ Rights and Resources.
rules.review_note: Official city page; the effective date is not stated, so status in_force is inferred from the page describing current enforcement.

result.doc_summary: Boston.gov page on the Housing Stability Notification Act (Boston City Code § 10-11.7). It requires all landlords ending a tenancy to deliver a Notice of Tenants' Rights and Resources with the notice to quit or non-renewal, and to submit the notice and tenant contact details to the City portal. Penalties are a warning for a first offense and $300 per day after that. A violation does not halt the eviction.
